data.body:
## Access config read with the admin identity — the ticket's open question is now answered

The Notes said the exact Submit rules could not be inspected from the bot. Read as `admin`:

`infra/gerrit/project.config` is the checked-in source of truth (pushed to `refs/meta/config`
by `infra/gerrit/setup-project.sh`, which overwrites it on every run). The grant is:

```
[access "refs/heads/*"]
	exclusiveGroupPermissions = submit
	submit = group Contributors
	submit = group Administrators
```

Live group membership:

| group | members |
|---|---|
| Contributors | `admin`, `JoeOakhartNava`, **`RebarBotNava`** |
| Service Users | `rebar-ci-bot`, **`rebar-review-bot`** |

## The root cause is narrower than this ticket assumed — and there are TWO bot accounts

The ticket reads this as a missing permission. It is better described as the wrong account
being used. `setup-project.sh` already provides for a landing bot:

```sh
CONTRIBUTOR_MEMBERS="${CONTRIBUTOR_MEMBERS:-RebarBotNava}"   # "the landing bot"
```

So `RebarBotNava` was created for exactly this purpose and is already in `Contributors`. The
account the agent workflow actually authenticates as — for `refs/for/main` pushes and for
`LLM-Review` votes — is `rebar-review-bot`, a different account that was never in that group.
Nothing is missing from the ACL; the designed lander simply is not the identity in use.

## This directly changes what AC2 permits

AC2 requires that granting Submit must not open a self-approval path. The project ACL grants
BOTH label permissions to `Service Users`:

```
	label-LLM-Review = -1..+1 group Service Users
	label-Verified   = -1..+1 group Service Users
```

`rebar-review-bot` is a Service User. It already holds both vote permissions, and it authors
the changes. Adding Submit to that same account would concentrate author, both gate voters,
and lander in one identity — the precise outcome AC2 forbids. There is no
`ignoreSelfApproval` on either label to fall back on.

`RebarBotNava` is in `Contributors` only, so it can Submit and can cast NEITHER gate label.
Routing submits through it preserves the separation AC2 is protecting, and needs no ACL
change at all — only a credential.

## What is actually missing

A credential for `RebarBotNava`. SSM holds `/rebar/prod/gerrit-admin-password`,
`/rebar/prod/gerrit-bot-token` (the review bot), `/rebar/prod/ci-gerrit-ssh-key`,
`/rebar/prod/gerrit-admin-ssh-key`, and `/rebar/prod/gerrit-ssh-host-ed25519-key`. There is
no parameter for the landing bot, which is why every submit this session fell back to the
admin password.

Escalated to the user, because the option originally chosen was to grant the review bot
Submit, and that choice was made before this separation-of-duties detail was known.
